pat.intro: GitLab needs an access token – a kind of password for apps – to upload changes, create repositories, open private repositories or load more often.
pat.howtoToggle: How do I create a token?
pat.step2: Under "Generate token", choose "Legacy token" — this integration does not support the newer "Fine-grained" token type.
pat.step3: Make sure the "api" scope is checked (the link above preselects it).
pat.step4: Choose a name and an expiration.
pat.step5: Generate the token. GitLab shows it only once — copy it now and paste it below.

result.alternative: Alternative, if the first one does not work

result.collaborationIntro: Send this link to everyone who should write along. They open the course in the editor and see every change immediately.
result.collaborationNote: Everyone with the link edits the same course. Whoever wants a version of their own uses “Make a copy” in the ⋮ menu.
result.externalIntro: This link opens the Markdown file from the web address in the editor.
result.externalNote: It only works as long as the file is publicly reachable on the internet.

result.snapshotIntro: Whoever opens this link gets the editor with a copy of the current file. Your course stays unchanged.
result.embedIntro: Paste this HTML code into your website. It shows the editor and the preview of the current file.
result.embedNote: Tip: replace “/embed/code/” in the address with “/embed/code/edit/” or “/embed/code/preview/” to show only the editor or only the preview.
result.longLinkWarning: Images and other files are not included, and very long links can be cut off by messengers or browsers. Test the link before you send it.
